dataset: TCGA-KIRC, 200 primary tumours, RNA-seq counts (STAR, unstranded) from the NCI Genomic Data Commons, imported in the LSMA Analysis Lab

input.expression_filter: more than 1 count per million in at least 20% of samples
warnings: There are 17,316 features for 200 samples. With far more features than samples a model can always find a pattern that fits the training data by chance; only the held-out test set shows whether it is real.

training.model: Cox regression with elastic-net penalty (lifelines), on the most variable features of the training patients

evaluation.validated_on: a held-out part of the same dataset; a second, independent cohort is the stronger test and is not available here

explanation.method: weights of the penalised Cox model

input.expression_filter: more than 1 count per million in at least 20% of samples
warnings: The classes are unbalanced (22 against 93). Accuracy is misleading here: a model that always answers the larger class already looks good. Read balanced accuracy and the ROC curve instead.
85 sample(s) with another value of 'stage' were left out.

There are 17,316 features for 115 samples. With far more features than samples a model can always find a pattern that fits the training data by chance; only the held-out test set shows whether it is real.

training.cross_validation: 5-fold, repeated 2 times, on the training samples
training.features_selected_per_fold: the 200 features with the largest F statistic, chosen inside every fold
training.tuning: settings tuned by an inner 3-fold cross-validation (nested)
warnings: Random forest scored highest, but 5 other model(s) cannot be told apart from it on these folds (Logistic regression (L2), Logistic regression (lasso), Logistic regression (elastic net)). Picking the top of a table like this is usually picking noise; prefer the simplest model among those that cannot be separated.
The best two models differ by less than the spread between folds. The choice between them is not meaningful.

evaluation.validated_on: a held-out part of the same dataset; a second, independent dataset is the stronger test and is not available here
warnings: Only 29 test samples: look at the interval (0.72 to 1.00), not at the single number.

explanation.method: permutation importance on the test samples (20 shuffles per feature), for the 200 features of the Random forest model
explanation.shap_values: not computed (permutation importance is used instead)
